page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance built on the Nitro System. The server is powered by dedicated Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, configured with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory is sized at 192.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per vCPU. The hardware platform operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

Integrated local storage is provided via 2850 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking throughput is anchored by a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation. Because the internal NVMe storage is configured as ephemeral instance store, data retention depends on node state, requiring external snapshotting or software-level replication patterns for stateful persistent workloads.

The dense combination of dedicated compute cores, large local NVMe storage, and 75 Gbps network interface provides hardware consolidation for I/O-intensive pipelines. The configuration is appropriate for relational and NoSQL databases, transactional processing, caching clusters, big data ETL tasks, and microservices requiring high baseline network bandwidth and rapid temporary storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance configured with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores on an Intel x86_64 architecture operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 2850 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth reaches 75 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput node communication without GPU accelerators. The dense combination of dedicated compute cores, fast local NVMe storage, and high networking throughput enables cost-effective resource consolidation for demanding environments. This profile makes m8idn.12xlarge well matched for distributed databases, intermediate data processing, high-capacity caching nodes, and concurrent backend services requiring high network capacity and low-latency ephemeral storage.
